thread:
incident-bot: :bell: Paging: p99 tail latency spike detected for streaming endpoints in eu-west-2. Auto-escalation to oncall.

alice (oncall): seeing massive p99 jump to ~3.8s on /v1/stream and stalled chunking, customers report timeouts. starting triage.

bob (eng-sre): grabbing logs now. any change pushed to routing policy in last 30m?

carol (eng-runtime): we pushed a weighted routing tweak 22m ago to favor local shards for throughput. rolling back is possible but will need coord with infra.

dave (product): potential customer impact: several enterprise clients reported degraded streaming; ticket #23456 flagged.

eva (support): confirming customer-reported stacktraces: client sees repeated 502s and stalled stream frames. attaching sample error: `stream stalled: recv timeout after 15s`

frank (cust-succ): raising priority with impacted clients, need ETA for mitigation.

alice (oncall): initial hypothesis: routing change caused hot-partitioning -> queueing -> tail latency. looking at router heatmap now.

bob (eng-sre): heatmap shows a handful of shards at 85-95% utilization in eu-west-2, other shards idle. sticky affinity plus new weight skew looks like hotkeys hitting same shard.

carol (eng-runtime): stack traces from router show repeated `ForwardingError: no healthy downstream` for those hot shards. streaming proxy is dropping keepalive.

alice (oncall): can we redirect traffic away from the hot shards temporarily? any quick policy we can push?

bob (eng-sre): yes — can flip a soft steer to next-best region or backoff to legacy egress pool. I'll prepare a patch to the routing service: set weight_multiplier=0.5 for affected shard group.

carol (eng-runtime): deploying a programmatic fallback now. command: ```
POST /admin/routing/patch
{
  "scope": "eu-west-2",
  "shard_group": "shard-17..20",
  "weight_multiplier": 0.5,
  "reason": "live mitigation - hot shard overflow"
}
```

bob (eng-sre): patch applied. watching metrics. p99 dropped from 3.8s -> 1.6s in the first minute. streaming stalls reduced but not gone.

alice (oncall): good sign. are there any fallback-induced mismatches? i.e., does fallback push too much cross-region traffic?

carol (eng-runtime): small increase in cross-region egress, but still under throttles. however we are seeing misroutes where cached KV prefixes are mismatched after fallback — resulting in duplicate cold starts.

bob (eng-sre): that could explain residual tail. KV cache miss count up 3x for that prefix. possibly the fallback exposed variants that don't share prefix keys.

alice (oncall): next step: tombstone the routing rule that caused the skew, and schedule a controlled rollback of the weighted tweak. bob/carol coordinate and confirm rollback window.

bob (eng-sre): starting tombstone now: `DELETE /admin/routing/rules/{rule-id-ef12}`. this will stop new policy evals but not hot sessions.

carol (eng-runtime): tombstone propagated. queue lengths on hot shards dropping slowly. p99 now ~900ms. streaming resumes for most clients.

frank (cust-succ): relaying to customers that we applied fallback and rolled back a policy; apologizing for interruption, they'll hold off on upgrades for next 24h.

eva (support): collecting case logs for affected customers. note: one client hit a retry storm that amplified load; recommend we ask them to apply client-side jitter and reduce aggressive reconnects.

alice (oncall): agreed — ask client to throttle reconnects. also we should run a short canary of the routing tweak with synthetic traffic before reapply.

dave (product): we need post-incident followup: include clearer gating on weight changes, add automated canary for routing weight flips and a rollback runbook.

bob (eng-sre): creating incident postmortem ticket now. immediate action items: 1) add preflight canary for routing weight; 2) add metric alert for shard skew > 4x baseline; 3) KV prefix affinity check after fallback.

carol (eng-runtime): for live mitigation, adding an autoscale buffer for streaming proxies in eu-west-2 to prevent drops if hot shard recurs. will monitor for 2 hours.

incident-bot: Incident severity updated to SEV-2. Oncall handover scheduled in 40m to bob (next).

alice (oncall): handing off to bob for long tail monitoring and postmortem writeup. I’ll update the customer comms channel. thanks team. :heart:

bob (eng-sre): taking over. I'll leave notes: root cause likely a routing weight bug that didn't respect prefix affinity; mitigation: tombstone rule + fallback redirect. next: deep dive on policy evaluator and unit tests for affinity invariants.

frank (cust-succ): will schedule a customer call tomorrow 10:00 CET.

alice (oncall): closing live page. if p99 creeps back up, reopen here or ring pager.

bob (eng-sre): copying key logs for postmortem: ```
[router] 2026-03-15T10:34:12Z WARN route_eval: rule ef12 applied weight=1.8 -> local_shard=17
[router] 2026-03-15T10:56:02Z ERROR forward: no healthy downstream shard=17 queue_len=512
[proxy]  2026-03-15T11:02:34Z INFO fallback: redirecting session -> egress-pool-2
```

carol (eng-runtime): saved heatmap snapshot to S3: s3://redwood-inference-ops/incidents/4498765432/heatmap-20260315.png

bob (eng-sre): postmortem draft will include timeline, mitigation steps, impact assessment (5 enterprise customers with degraded streams ~20-40 minutes), and followups. assigning owners in the ticket.

incident-bot: Incident resolved and archived. Severity downgraded to SEV-3 after follow-ups scheduled.
